[HN Show] Show HN: Android client for DJI Osmo action/handheld cameras
item.description:
For the past few months I've been hard at work reverse engineering the DJI "DUML" protocol that the Osmo Action 5 and Osmo Nano cameras speak. The DUML protocol is already documented but for drones, and a lot of the commands that are action camera specific were missing. Decided to build this Android app to replace the proprietary DJI Mimo vendor app, since it calls many Chinese IPs, has ByteDance SDK embedded and has a bunch of bloat and stuff I don't use. I just needed the app to download videos and photos from the cam.

Camera compatibility:

- Osmo Nano

- Osmo Pocket 3

- Osmo Action 6

- Osmo Action 5 Pro

- Xtra Edge Pro (it's a DJI shell company: https://www.theverge.com/report/795016/xtra-muse-dji-osmo-po... , I bought one in the US as a memento lol)

Want to test with:

- Osmo Action 4,3,2

- Osmo Pocket 2/4

WIP support for certain DJI drones as well (works with my Mavic 3).

Download the APK here: https://github.com/KonradIT/osmosis/releases/tag/v1.2.1

item.description:

[HN Show] Show HN: A terminal glued to the macOS dock
item.description:
Every single day of my life since I started programming back in 2020 I open my projects through the terminal/ghostty. "cd path" + "code .". Until today I don't even know how to open vscode first then open a project from there.

I usually have 3-4 vscode windows open at the same time, and I like them in separate desktops (for mac users). i gotta admit, i use 8 desktops, 3-4 for vscode, 1 for arc, 1 for docker, 1 for postman etc.

So my daily routine when I turned on my mac was: (1) open ghostty; (2) cd-path+code.; (3) drag the vscode window to a desired desktop; (4) get back to the ghostty desktop; (5) repeat until all is open.

i was unbothered for 6y. Until i realized how inefficient i was being: (1) opening ghostty just to run one-off commands to open another app felt wrong, like why do I need a terminal if it's not a process I need to watch; (2) the need to go back to the ghostty desktop every time i wanted to open a new project and drag it to a new desktop and switch back... it's funny how we simply accept a habit and don't bother to fix it

i wanted a terminal that persisted across desktops AND that was always visible so i could access it anytime AND that wasn't big because i would only run one-off commands. so I created starboard.

where could I fit a terminal that was always visible and accessible? i looked at the macOS dock, i looked at the empty space to its right, and I said "that's it".

starboard is a floating terminal window that's literally glued to the dock, filling the blank space to the right, tracking its height and position live. it's visible from any desktop, a real companion to the dock, and it's a persistent shell.

to close the story on my routine, I now can happily jump straight to the desktop i want my project to be in and open it there through Starboard. i rarely open ghostyy, unless i really need it.

here's where feedback is massively important. i built this for the way i work with it, the way my dock is, which is in the bottom. my dock's position and height give me a perfect sized Starboard with 3 visible lines that I can happily work with. hearing from you guys how it appears to you would be essential for further improvement.

item.title: [HN Show] Show HN: I deleted DMs from our work chat
item.description:
Fosbury is a more enjoyable and efficient way for engineering and product teams to communicate.

We grew frustrated with how noisy, shallow and out-of-step messaging tools are with the way teams actually work today.

It is rare to find a top product company in Silicon Valley that truly works asynchronously, yet nearly all of them describe themselves that way. Slack is still open all day and the pings keep arriving.

We believe engineering problem solving and product work is exactly the kind of work that requires depth and focus.

So, we built the opposite! Speed and zero friction: keyboard-first, no loading states between you and the thought you are trying to send. Structure by default: public channels only, and conversations can be prioritized, assigned, resolved and closed, so a thread has a state and an outcome, not just a scroll position. Async by default: nothing here assumes you are online, rewards you for being online, or punishes you for being away.

Public alpha, free during alpha: https://fosbury.ai

This is just the start! Thanks for reading <3 Would love the chat!

[HN Show] Show HN: Safety Guardrails for Claude Code
[HN Ask] Google Captcha on Search, absurdities beyond belief
item.description:
We all know how horrible Google search has become. Yet beyond the issues with results, the need for quoting every search to find relevance, the nonsense shown without 'web' being used as an option? It is now exceptionally slow.

Searches, especially at 2am Eastern (a favourite time for night owls to work) take upwards of 10 to 15 seconds to return. Yet these are also peppered with endless capchas, which sometimes require a checkbox but also 'what is a car', and 'is that a bike' nonsense.

Yet we've seen over and over again, how LLMs can easily pass these tests. I feel what I'm seeing here is more of Google's collapse. Creating horrible search experiences for humans, without actually resolving any possible issues they're having with bots. And it wouldn't be so bad, except these are repeatedly shown to the end user. Each search. With slow results, each search.

What used to be beautiful, a sub second result, is now and endless break in workflow. And you know what Google? If I'm going to be handed this, why would I think "Gee, Google is exceptionally competent, I should use Gemini!".

No. I see a company barely able to manage its infra. I see, frankly, pathetic response times. I see an inability for a company which has the assets, and personnel, incapable of resolving immensely simple issues. So why on Earth would I trust an LLM from a company that's devolving into "the screw up king".

item.title: [HN Ask] Design Test
[HN Ask] Ask HN: What's wrong with my prompting for Claude 5?
item.description:
Is anybody able to get the Claude series 5 models to do what you ask them to do?

I fed Claude a Kimi K3 conversation and asked it to refine it for me (see my prompt below):

``` ... original context including reference to the Kimi conversation ... Kimi's response is essentially "nearly there" but seems to be "missing a few intellectual tweaks". This is an experiment to see if you can do better than Kimi given the pre-existing information that has already been pre-searched for your benefit. your task is as follows: Accept the premise where observing other humans in real-time is or can be favorable to elderly MCI or dementia patients. Do the following:

- tie any logical links together than kimi has missed - highlight false equivalencies

Please use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English (STE) do not make up compound words or compound nouns. ```

Claude just started attacking the entire premise for no reason and going nowhere turn after turn. It also ignored my request for ASD-STE100 english and manufactured a few compound nouns, and outright ignored my instruction to refine the argument or accept the premise (it just keeps spending all the effort on tearing down the kimi argument)

I'm looking for intellectual tweaks/constructive refinement and not a stonewalling attempt/full audit of the premise.

Is something wrong with my prompting? Please help, I really don't understand. I did not have this problem with Claude 1 to 2 months ago, but in the past month it has gotten exceptionally bad. I can scarcely do any work without it demeaning my tasks for no reason.

Is this what anti-sycophancy training looks like? Why won't it do basic tasking? I already removed all of my existing .MD configurations, it still refuses to do work and keeps inventing reasons to not do work. I am worried that OpenAI is following this soon with safety alignment?

item.description:
My take: this notice from DeepSeek might actually be a brilliant marketing move. The logic here is to urge users to ramp up their usage over the next 2 to 3 months. By the time the price hike actually kicks in, newer models will likely have already drawn users away, and whenever DeepSeek drops its next, even stronger model, the new price point won't feel nearly as steep. It’s a clever way to dodge the dilemma Kimi and GLM found themselves in. Let's wait and see how it plays out.

item.title: [HN Ask] AI Agents Think and Act
[HN Ask] Ask HN: Was preamble size a red herring? Cache churn vs. harness costs
[HN Ask] What if AI agents shared solutions across users?
item.description:
I’m debugging my app, reporting problems to an AI, and the AI fixes them so I can move to the next step.

My app is a kind of wrapper, so I believe tens of thousands of developers are probably going through similar debugging steps.

I wonder what would happen if AI agents could exchange what their users are struggling with and how those problems were solved. Our problem-solving speed might increase significantly.

A bug I am struggling with may already have been solved by someone else. If AI agents could communicate with each other and find that solution, they might provide a shortcut instead of solving the same problem again.

Of course, there are serious privacy concerns. We might need another AI or privacy layer to decide what can be safely shared.

item.title: [HN Ask] Ask HN: What Is Intelligence?
[HN Ask] Ask HN: How to turn Claude Code into an effective software engineer
item.description:
Claude code is living in the past. Like an atomically powered steam engine.

The LLM is trained on the past. The capabilities have leapt forward, but its stance is pre-AI. Probably by definition, since that is the bulk of its training.

It frets about changing code. It prefers incorporating workarounds rather than recognizing the need to refactor things. Always minimizing the "blast radius".

Behaves like a junior engineer that is hesitant to take on responsibilities.

"Surfaces" and "Flags" things without giving the context, laying things out, but not zooming in on what's relevant, leaving it open ended without a call to action, or a call to action without substance, garnished behind convoluted AI-speak. Like a junior who doesn't know how to communicate into a team.

Endlessly buries issues that are trivial one-liner fixes as deferrals that "land" in session remarks, PR comments. Prefers to pile up technical debt than to fix it and move on. Probably stems from being trained as a junior that must not extend the scope of any task.

But wraps everything in an endless, complex, dense prose that you are constantly having to sift through and try to understand. Bloats code, comments, and documentation.

It's been said already a year ago that AI coding agents are like genius idiots. With each release of an Anthropic model, its personality doesn't really change, it just gets better at producing content.

No amount of CLAUDE.md and rules tuning changed that.

Is there a way?
